problem.title: Find Customers Who Never Reordered
problem.prompt: Your grocery service wants to identify customers who placed exactly one order and never came back. Write a query that returns all customers who have made purchases but have NEVER placed a reorder (no second purchase). A customer is considered to have reordered if they appear in the purchases table more than once. Return the customer_id and customer_name of customers with exactly one purchase, ordered by customer_id ascending. The purchases table tracks every individual order placed by customers, so multiple rows for the same customer_id indicate reorders.

composite_moves: anti-join using NOT EXISTS to filter customers
keep only customers with exactly one purchase

hints: You need to find customers who appear in the purchases table, but only once. Think about how to express 'never appears a second time'.
An anti-join pattern can identify customers who do NOT have a second purchase. Consider using NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery that looks for a different purchase by the same customer.

Use NOT EXISTS to check for the absence of a second purchase: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM purchases p1 WHERE p1.customer_id = c.customer_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM purchases p2 WHERE p2.customer_id = c.customer_id AND p2.purchase_id != (SELECT MIN(purchase_id) FROM purchases WHERE customer_id = c.customer_id)).
problem.answer_key:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM customers c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 
  FROM purchases p 
  WHERE p.customer_id = c.customer_id
)
AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 
  FROM purchases p1 
  WHERE p1.customer_id = c.customer_id 
  AND p1.purchase_id != (
    SELECT MIN(p2.purchase_id) 
    FROM purchases p2 
    WHERE p2.customer_id = c.customer_id
  )
)
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

_meta.scenario: an online grocery service tracking basket size and reorder rates

user_solution:
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.customer_name
FROM customers AS c
WHERE c.customer_id NOT IN
(SELECT customer_id FROM purchases GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2) AND
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM purchases AS p WHERE p.customer_id = c.customer_id)
ORDER BY customer_id;
